title: Reset algorithm doesn't work in form-associated custom elements

labels.name: topic: custom elements
labels.description: Relates to custom elements (as defined in DOM and HTML)

body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

There are 3 places in the specification where the [reset algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-form-reset-control) is triggered:
1) The [reset](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-form-reset) algorithm, which resets the state of all form participants to default values
   > 2. If reset is true, then invoke the [reset algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-form-reset-control) of each [resettable element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#category-reset) whose [form owner](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#form-owner) is form.

2) The [create an element for a token](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#create-an-element-for-the-token) algorithm, whose task is to create an element for the HTML parser.
   > 13. If element is a [resettable element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#category-reset), invoke its [reset algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-form-reset-control). (This initializes the element's [value](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fe-value) and [checkedness](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-fe-checked) based on the element's attributes.)

3) The [reactivate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#reactivate-a-document) algorithm, which is used to update the document
   > 1. [For each](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-iterate) formControl of form controls in document with an [autofill field name](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#autofill-field-name) of "[off](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#attr-fe-autocomplete-off)", invoke the [reset algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-form-reset-control) for formControl.

The first case works fine, no questions about it, no matter whether via a button or via the [reset()](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#dom-form-reset) API, it works well and the `formResetCallback` hook makes itself known.

The second case fails, it does not call the `formResetCallback` hook (detailed below).

The third case also does not execute the `formResetCallback` hook, the conditions for its execution are unachievable (due with form-associated custom elements).

---

As a small test, I made this example for the [create an element for a token](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#create-an-element-for-the-token) case:

```html
<script>
customElements.define("my-input", class extends HTMLElement {
  static formAssociated = true;
  connectedCallback() {
     console.log("my-input connected");
  }
  formResetCallback() {
     console.log("my-input performed formResetCallback");
  }
});
</script>
<form>
  <my-input></my-input>
</form>
```

And if you run such html file with a custom element that has the [reset algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-form-reset-control):

> The [reset algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-form-reset-control) for [form-associated custom elements](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#form-associated-custom-element) is to [enqueue a custom element callback reaction](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction) with the element, callback name "formResetCallback", and an empty argument list.

Then we will not see the called `formResetCallback` hook, but this should work (yes, we are talking about the second case, when the HTML parser [creates an element for the token](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#create-an-element-for-the-token) and after run [reset algorithm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-form-reset-control) in step 13).

I checked this in the latest Chrome and Firefox, the hook is not called. What's wrong?

---

Maybe problem is in this note, why implementations don't correspond the step 13:
> A [custom element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#custom-element) possesses the ability to respond to certain occurrences by running author code:
> - When the form owner of a [form-associated custom element](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/custom-elements.html#form-associated-custom-element) is [reset](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#concept-form-reset), its formResetCallback is called.

By the way, [that wpt test](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/ab57bca30a4845855ea43fb318a9802beac8508f/custom-elements/form-associated/form-reset-callback.html) is too old, it does not check what I am talking about.

---

What do you say editors?
